I: › [ I ] to move in a way that is not regular or normal, especially making sudden movements backwards or forwards or from side to side
搖晃，晃動；（尤指）突然傾斜
I + adv/prep: › [ I + adv/prep ] to act or continue in away that is uncontrolled and not regular, often with sudden changes

NONE: › a sudden movement or change that is not smooth or normal
突然的傾斜（搖晃或改變）

example: The train lurched forward and some of the people standing fell over.
火車突然向前晃動了一下，一些站著的人跌倒了。
We seem to lurch from crisis to crisis.
我們似乎總是跌跌撞撞，危機不斷。
She just lurches from one bad relationship to another.
她情路坎坷。
The truck gave a sudden lurch as it was hit by a strong gust of wind.
一陣強風襲來，貨車突然搖晃了一下。
The party's lurch (= sudden change) to the left will lose it a lot of support.
該黨突然轉向左派將會失去很多人的支持。

C usually singular: C2 [ C usually singular ] the quality or power that something or someone has that makes it, him, or her attractive
C: › [ C ] an artificial insect or other small animal that is put on the end of a fishing line to attract fish

NONE: C2 to persuade someone to do something or go somewhere by offering them something exciting

example: the lure of fame/power/money
名譽／權力／金錢的誘惑
She was lured into the job by the offer of a high salary.
她受高薪誘惑接受了那份工作。
He had lured his victim to a deserted house.
他將受害者引誘到一座廢棄的房子。
Supermarket chains try to lure customers with price discounts.
連鎖超級市場試圖用折扣來吸引顧客。

NONE: › a brand name for a type of thread that looks shiny, like metal, or cloth made from this thread
盧勒克斯金屬細線；盧勒克斯金屬質地

example: a gold/silver Lurex top
金絲／銀絲上裝

NONE: › an illness or disease, especially one that is not serious
疾病；（尤指不嚴重的）小病

example: He's got the dreaded lurgy.
他染上了那種令人色變的疾病。

NONE: › (especially of a description) shocking because involving violence, sex, or immoral activity
（尤指描述）駭人的，令人毛骨悚然的

example: You can read all the lurid details of the affair in today's paper.
今天的報紙上對這件事駭人聽聞的細節描寫得淋漓盡致。
That's a very lurid shade of lipstick she's wearing.
她口紅抹得太豔了。

I usually + adv/prep: › [ I usually + adv/prep ] to wait or move in a secret way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong
（尤指爲攻擊某人或做壞事而）潛伏，隱蔽，悄悄移動
› [ I usually + adv/prep ] (of an unpleasant feeling or quality) to exist although it is not always noticeable
（不好的感覺或特徵）潛伏，潛藏

I: › [ I ] informal internet & telecoms to spend time in a chat room or on a social media website and read what other people have posted (= written or added) without posting anything yourself
在（網上）聊天室裡潛水；隱身進入（網上）聊天室

example: Someone was lurking in the shadows.
有人藏在黑影裡。
Why are you lurking around in the hallway?
你幹嗎在走廊裡鬼鬼祟祟的？
Danger lurks around every corner.
每個角落裡都潛伏著危險。
It seems that old prejudices are still lurking beneath the surface.
在表像的背後似乎依然潛藏著舊有的偏見。

NONE: › someone who reads the messages in a chat room without taking part
（網際網路上聊天室裡的）潛水者

example: They spend every evening together - I think it might be lurve.
他們每天晚上都在一起——我想他們可能相愛了。
